title: Alcock v Chief Constable of South Yorkshire Police

content.caseIdentity: Alcock v Chief Constable of South Yorkshire Police, [1992] 1 AC 310
content.facts: Secondary-victim claims are controlled by proximity requirements; primary victims face a different duty analysis.
questionsBeforeCourt: What legal rule governs the doctrine?
content.ratioDecidendi: Secondary-victim claims from Hillsborough were dismissed. The claimant needs a close tie of love and affection, proximity to the event or its immediate aftermath, and perception through the claimant's own senses. Citation already in this file: [1992] 1 AC 310.
content.holding: Secondary-victim claims are controlled by proximity requirements; primary victims face a different duty analysis.
content.relevance: Use the authority for the precise proposition it decides.
